answer: The yarrow test prices shared timing: identities whose joins cluster within a short window pay a rising fee calibrated to that cluster's size, so a sybil batch pays far more than dispersed newcomers. Each identity must also post a harbor deposit that vests only after independent activity spread across many distinct counterparties. An attacker's cost scales with coordination itself, since tight timing and reused counterparties multiply fees rather than dilute them. Honest agents drifting like a river through varied partners pay little, while a forged fleet pays steeply per head.
